title: Don't believe the GenAI hype—learn from it instead, say researchers
excerpt: When is a hype bubble more than just a bubble? When it becomes a mass, real-time learning event. New research published in the Academy of Management Journal by Anna Brattstrom, a professor at the University of St Andrews Business School, and Hassan Hamadi, a PhD student at Lund University, aimed to understand the hype around generative AI.
content_html:
When is a hype bubble more than just a bubble? When it becomes a mass, real-time learning event. New research published in the Academy of Management Journal by Anna Brattstrom, a professor at the University of St Andrews Business School, and Hassan Hamadi, a PhD student at Lund University, aimed to understand the hype around generative AI.

The team looked at 200,000 X posts from the first five months after ChatGPT was launched, gathering and analyzing reactions to the new tool—from abject dismissals ("this is complete nonsense") to evangelism ("this is completely revolutionary!"). What they discovered was "an unusual event" that didn't follow the usual patterns of hype cycles.

"Hype is typically seen as a speculative bubble," Brattstrom says. "A company projects a big vision, and the rest of us absorb it." But the conversation around ChatGPT was different. "It broke that pattern. Because anyone could use it straight away, the hype and conversations on social media became a way for us all to collectively teach ourselves what the technology could and couldn't do."

In this instance, it appears that social media—counter to its reputation for polarizing debate and amplifying outlandish statements—actually brought moderation, nuance and insight to the discussion. "Once enough knowledge had accumulated, the wildest predictions got vetted out. So the hype helped us reach a more sensible understanding of generative AI, while still keeping us interested in it."

Sharing insights with the Academy of Management, Brattstrom and Hamadi say their research points to ways in which organizations can use hype around accessible technologies, both as an early-warning system and as a learning engine. They advise managers to monitor public experimentation, not just expert commentary; avoid jumping to premature conclusions about a new technology's value; and provide employees with opportunities to safely try out and learn from new tools.

The conversation around generative AI is rapidly evolving, and the researchers say it would be a mistake to dismiss public discussion and social media hype as "just noise." "The hype is a learning opportunity, where something valuable would emerge from the public—like 'wisdom of the crowd'—because social media enables a diversity of perspectives to gain traction, get corrected and be amplified," Hamadi says.

Being proactive in using and understanding new technologies is key, Brattstrom says, so that people are empowered to "take part in the unfolding conversations about its benefits, limitations and risks."

Publication details

Hassan Md. Hamadi et al, ChatGPT, a Hype That Teaches: Generative AI and the Collective Accumulation of Technology Literacy on Social Media, Academy of Management Journal (2026). DOI: 10.5465/amj.2024.0536

content_html_zh:
什么时候炒作泡沫不仅仅是泡沫？ 当它成为一个大规模的实时学习活动时。 圣安德鲁斯大学商学院教授 Anna Brattstrom 和隆德大学博士生 Hassan Hamadi 在《管理学院杂志》上发表了一项新研究，旨在了解围绕生成式人工智能的炒作。

该团队查看了 ChatGPT 推出后前五个月的 200,000 个帖子，收集并分析了对新工具的反应 - 从卑鄙的解雇（“这完全是无稽之谈”）到传播福音（“这完全是革命性的！”）。 他们发现的是“一个不寻常的事件”，不遵循炒作周期的通常模式。

“炒作通常被视为投机泡沫，”布拉特斯特罗姆说。 “一家公司制定了一个宏伟的愿景，而我们其他人则吸收它。” 但围绕 ChatGPT 的讨论却有所不同。 “它打破了这种模式。 因为任何人都可以立即使用它，社交媒体上的炒作和对话成为我们所有人集体自学该技术可以做什么和不能做什么的一种方式。”

在这种情况下，社交媒体似乎与它两极分化辩论和放大古怪言论的名声相反，实际上给讨论带来了温和、细微差别和洞察力。 “一旦积累了足够的知识，最疯狂的预测就会被淘汰。 因此，炒作帮助我们对生成人工智能有了更明智的理解，同时仍然让我们保持对它的兴趣。”

布拉特斯特罗姆和哈马迪与管理学院分享了他们的见解，他们的研究指出了组织可以利用围绕无障碍技术的炒作的方式，既可以作为预警系统，也可以作为学习引擎。 他们建议管理者监控公共实验，而不仅仅是专家评论；避免对新技术的价值过早下结论；并为员工提供安全尝试和学习新工具的机会。

围绕生成人工智能的讨论正在迅速发展，研究人员表示，将公众讨论和社交媒体炒作视为“只是噪音”是错误的。 哈马迪说：“炒作是一个学习机会，公众会发现一些有价值的东西，比如‘群体的智慧’，因为社交媒体使多样化的观点能够获得关注、得到纠正和放大。”

布拉特斯特罗姆说，积极主动地使用和理解新技术是关键，这样人们就有能力“参与有关其好处、局限性和风险的不断展开的对话”。
